stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy with two separate dispensing windows is reviewing its counseling-rights signage. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A single sign at the store entrance satisfies the requirement for the whole pharmacy.
The letters may be any size provided the sign is legible from the counter.
A sign must be posted conspicuously adjacent to each area where prescriptions are dispensed.
The sign must be at least 11 inches in height by 14 inches in width.
The sign must be printed in both English and Spanish.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.18(7) requires a sign of not less than 11 inches in height by 14 inches in width, posted conspicuously adjacent to each area where prescriptions are dispensed, informing customers of their right to counseling, with letters not less than one half inch in height and specified wording.

choice_analysis.A: A single entrance sign does not meet the adjacent-to-each-area requirement.
choice_analysis.B: A minimum letter height of one half inch is prescribed.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: adjacent to each dispensing area, so two windows need two signs.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: 11 inches by 14 inches is the stated minimum.
choice_analysis.E: The regulation prescribes wording, not a bilingual requirement.

related_facts: The prescribed wording tells patients they have the right to know about proper use and effects and to ask the pharmacist.
explanation.mpje_trap: Two dispensing windows are two areas, and both the sign size and the letter height are prescribed.

reasoning_steps: Count the areas where prescriptions are dispensed
Check the prescribed sign dimensions and letter height
